subject: ArcadiaCare security questionnaire & evidence: SSQ answers + KMS custody
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@arcadiacare.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2029-03-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: ArcadiaCare security questionnaire and evidence request

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement & InfoSec at ArcadiaCare reviewed Redwood's public materials and sent over a security questionnaire focused on PII handling, subprocessors, and cross-border flows. I'm attaching the ArcadiaCare_SSQ_20290315.pdf with the specific asks.

Top items we need for our audit:
- Single-page data flow diagram showing transit & residency for PII (ingest -> model -> logs/telemetry)
- List of subprocessors and geographies where tokenized/processed data may move
- KMS custody model and whether customer keys or Redwood-managed keys are used; if customer keys are supported, we'd like attestation of key isolation and export controls
- Retention/retention-by-environment (prod vs. dev) and logs exportability

Can you send initial answers and any evidence (diagrams, attestation, or a short write-up) by EOD Friday? We are trying to close security review before our procurement committee meets next Wednesday.

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
Head of InfoSec Programs
ArcadiaCare

Attachment: ArcadiaCare_SSQ_20290315.pdf (application/pdf)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@arcadiacare.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-03-16T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ArcadiaCare security questionnaire and evidence request

Hi Elena —

Appreciate the clear asks and the SSQ. We've pulled together initial answers below and attached a response packet. Short summary up front: Redwood supports customer-managed keys (KMS) for Dedicated and Private deployments and uses a Redwood-managed KMS for standard Hosted API with strict access controls. We are happy to provide an attestation for key custody and a single-page data flow diagram.

Deliverables attached:
- Redwood_SSQ_Response_ArcadiaCare_20290316.pdf (answers mapped to your questions)
- Preliminary data flow diagram (page 3 of the PDF)

Quick answers to your bullets:
- Data flow diagram: included in the packet (ingest -> inference runtime -> temporary KV cache -> persisted telemetry in encrypted object store). We highlight differences between Hosted and Dedicated.
- Subprocessors: list included; primary compute is in US regions, certain telemetry aggregation and monitoring vendors operate in US/EU.
- KMS custody: For Hosted, Redwood manages keys in a hardened KMS with strict role-based access and split-key escrow. For Dedicated/Private, customers may provide keys via customer KMS or HSM (we have an integration checklist).
- Retention: Default hosted telemetry retention is 90 days; logs exports on request for compliance. Dedicated/Private retention is configurable and contractually enforceable.

Action items:
- @kimberly_park: can you prepare the KMS custody attestation (short doc) addressing key isolation, no-export guarantees, and HSM options?
- @connor_obrien: please review the attached SSQ responses for any red flags before I send the full packet to Elena.

Elena — I'll follow up with the attestation as a separate attachment once Kimberly confirms. If you need the information mapped to specific SSQ keys (e.g., 2.1, 3.4), call that out and we'll add a crosswalk.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_SSQ_Response_ArcadiaCare_20290316.pdf (application/pdf)

Key bullets to include: no export without customer authorization, role-based access logs, HSM-backed key protection, quarterly key custody audit schedule, and how we handle key revocation during offboarding.

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>

Date: 2029-03-16T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FW: ArcadiaCare security questionnaire — KMS attestation request

Marissa & Connor,

Attached is a draft KMS attestation (Redwood_KMS_Attestation_Draft_20290316.pdf). Highlights:
- Hosted: Redwood-managed keys are stored in a tenant-isolated key vault; access limited to a small subset of SRE/KeyOps with just-in-time access using ephemeral IAM tokens.
- Dedicated/Private: customers may supply keys via supported KMS/HSM integrations; Redwood never exports customer key material from the customer's key boundary.
- Revocation: documented revocation playbook with verifiable audit logs; offboarding includes key rotation and crypto-scheme teardown.
- Audits: we run quarterly key custody reviews internally and annually use a third-party assessor for attestation on request.

Connor — please confirm the phrasing around "quarterly review" and the list of roles with access. I based the role list on current KeyOps roster but can redact names.

Kimberly

Attachment: Redwood_KMS_Attestation_Draft_20290316.pdf (application/pdf)
